cse-2018-cs-49.approach: Plot the function on a 4-variable K-map, list **all** prime implicants (largest groups of 1s and don't-cares), then find the minterms that are covered by exactly one prime implicant — those prime implicants are essential. Don't-cares help form groups but never need covering.

steps.title: Plot the 1s and don't-cares
steps.body: Rows are $PQ$ and columns $RS$, both in Gray-code order $00, 01, 11, 10$ (so the outer rows and columns are adjacent). Each cell's small number is its minterm index $8P+4Q+2R+S$.

steps.title: Find every prime implicant
steps.body:
Grow each group as large as possible using 1s and X's:

| Prime implicant | Cells |
|---|---|
| $\bar Q \bar S$ | 0, 2, 8, 10 (four corners) |
| $P \bar Q$ | 8, 9, 10, 11 |
| $\bar Q R$ | 2, 3, 10, 11 |
| $P \bar S$ | 8, 10, 12, 14 |
| $\bar P Q S$ | 5, 7 |
| $\bar P R S$ | 3, 7 |

None can grow further (e.g. $\bar P Q S$ would need 1 or 13, which are 0s).

steps.title: Find minterms covered by only one prime implicant
steps.body:
Check each **minterm** (not don't-care):

- $m_0$: only $\bar Q \bar S$ → essential
- $m_2$: $\bar Q \bar S$, $\bar Q R$
- $m_5$: only $\bar P Q S$ → essential
- $m_7$: $\bar P Q S$, $\bar P R S$
- $m_9$: only $P \bar Q$ → essential
- $m_{11}$: $P \bar Q$, $\bar Q R$

steps.title: Count the essential prime implicants
steps.body: The essential prime implicants are $\bar Q \bar S$, $\bar P Q S$ and $P \bar Q$ — **3** of them. Together they already cover every minterm (0, 2 | 5, 7 | 9, 11), so the minimal SOP is $F = \bar Q \bar S + \bar P Q S + P \bar Q$.

answer.value: **3** essential prime implicants ($\bar Q \bar S$, $\bar P Q S$, $P \bar Q$)

cse-2018-cs-49.shortcut: Look only at the 1-cells with few neighbours: $m_0$, $m_5$ and $m_9$ each sit in exactly one maximal group, so each forces its own essential PI. $m_2$, $m_7$, $m_{11}$ have two choices each.
pitfalls: Counting $P\bar S$ or $\bar Q R$ as essential because they cover don't-cares — a PI is essential only if it is the sole cover of a **minterm**.
Missing the four-corner group $\bar Q \bar S$ by not treating the map as wrapping around.
cse-2018-cs-49.verification: Algebraic check of each essential PI: $\bar Q\bar S$ is the only PI with $Q=0, S=0$ containing $m_0 = 0000$; $\bar P Q S$ is the only PI with $P=0, Q=1, S=1$ ($m_5 = 0101$ has neighbours 1, 4, 7, 13 — only 7 is non-zero); $m_9 = 1001$ has neighbours 1, 8, 11, 13 — only the group $8,9,10,11$ contains it.
